newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Poor May inflation was exceptional-Portugal Min.
newsitem.headline: Poor May inflation was exceptional-Portugal Min.

text.p: Portuguese Finance Minister Antonio Sousa Franco said that the disappointing 0.7 percent monthly increase in inflation in May was an exceptional result that should not be repeated.

"We had occasional factors concerning agricultural and food products (to blame for the figure), which I hope will stop their negative effects during these months of June and July," he told Reuters Financial Television (RFTV) in an interview at a conference in Frankfurt.
"The average annual inflation is heading down towards the target (for 1997)," he added. The government has set an official target for inflation of between 2.25 and 2.50 percent for 1997.

Consumer prices rose by 0.7 percent in May, compared with 0.2 percent in April and 0.5 percent in May 1996. Average annual inflation dropped to 3.0 percent in May from 3.1 percent in April and 3.4 percent in May 1996.
